mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member states: notarize in origin -> issue Hague Apostille certificate by originating state competent authority -> certified Korean translation -> submit to Korean Court Registration Office or KoFIU. Non-member states: notarize in origin -> obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate in the origin country -> certified Korean translation -> submit. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Secretary of State, Companies House, Registry of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: On Apostille route: notarize or certify as required in origin -> Apostille only -> certified Korean translation. On Consular route: legalize by Korean diplomatic mission in origin only -> certified Korean translation. Never use apostille and consularization together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Authorizing Formation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the ultimate parent company, notarized in the jurisdiction of the parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member states: notarized board resolution -> apostille from competent authority of origin -> certified Korean translation. Non-member states: notarized board resolution -> consular legalization by Korean consulate/embassy in origin -> certified Korean translation. The chosen route must follow the origin country's convention membership only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Proposed Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public or notary in the origin jurisdiction for foreign incorporators, with Korean translation if executed abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed abroad: notarize -> apostille (member state) or consular legalization (non-member state) -> certified Korean translation. If executed in Korea: notarize before Korean notary, no apostille or consular legalization required for Korean domestic filing. The dual foreign authentication routes remain mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution where the UBO maintains the primary account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille states: bank signs under notary -> apostille by origin competent authority -> certified Korean translation. Non-apostille states: bank signs under notary -> Korean consular legalization in origin -> certified Korean translation. The two authentication routes cannot be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, signatories and counterparties must be screened before incorporation against the UN Security Council sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and the Korean government-designated financing of terrorism list. PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including family members and close associates, with automated name-matching in Korean, English and transliterated Chinese. Matches must trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, ongoing transaction monitoring, and filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report with KoFIU where required. Negative news screening and beneficial ownership re-verification must occur at least every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Court Registration Office, Internet Registration Office (I-ROS; iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in Hangeul and must include the legal suffix Chusik Hoesa or Jusik Hoesa. A foreign-language name is not permitted as the primary registered name; foreign words must be phonetically transliterated into Hangeul. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) distinctive identifier, (2) business description, (3) corporate form suffix, and (4) optional English/Chinese trade alias disclosed to tax and banking authorities. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name in Korea and must not contain restricted tokens unless prior approval is obtained from the relevant ministry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Court Registration Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection within two weeks with the same registration official, attaching the name search certificate and explaining why the proposed name is distinct and not misleading. If the objection is denied, the applicant may file an immediate appeal with the local District Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The appeal must specify the registry reference, the statutory basis for clearance, and any ministerial approval obtained for sensitive tokens. A parallel new name search should be filed while the appeal is pending to preserve timeline. All appeal documents must be in Korean or accompanied by certified translations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Korea must be a real physical location capable of receiving official mail and being inspected. Pure virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally rejected by the National Tax Service (NTS) for business registration and by regulated banks for corporate account opening in the tax advisory and cross-border consultancy sector. A serviced office with a dedicated private desk, physical signage, mail logs and staff presence may be accepted, but the NTS and KoFIU require full access to books, records and personnel. For ISIC 7020 tax structuring consultancy, a virtual office is high-risk and likely to be refused for value-added tax and anti-money laundering purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: valid lease agreement, Hangeul signage, physical mail reception, dedicated workspace, proof of occupancy, availability of responsible officer during business hours, on-site access to statutory records and accounting books. Quantified risk: standard physical office in commercial building - 15% likelihood of unannounced inspection within 12 months; serviced/shared office - 40%; virtual/mailbox address or inconsistent sign - 75%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Book III on Commercial Companies, particularly Articles 289, 291, 295, 303, 312, 314, 317, 383, 390, and 393; Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident capital participation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Korean Corporation Registration Application Form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The articles of incorporation may fix any positive capital amount, and the entire subscription price must be paid in or deposited before the incorporation meeting is held. No blocked escrow account is required by law, but the subscriber or promoter must place the subscription money in a Korean bank or securities company account in the name of the company or the promotor, and a bank certificate of deposit must be produced to the registration court. For non-resident shareholders, the foreign capital contribution must additionally comply with the reporting regime under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA, INC., a stock corporation incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. The directors of the company held a duly convened meeting at the registered office on [DATE], at [TIME]. The following directors attended: [DIRECTOR NAMES], constituting a lawful quorum. After due deliberation, the board unanimously adopted the following resolutions: 1. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company be and is hereby fixed at [COMPLETE ADDRESS], [CITY], Republic of Korea, which shall be recorded in the commercial register and serve as the principal administrative seat, corporate tax domicile, and legal address for service of process. 2. SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that the total issued shares of the company are [NUMBER] shares divided into the classes authorized in the articles of incorporation, and that the total paid-in share capital is KRW [AMOUNT]. The board certifies that all subscription amounts have been fully paid into the company's capital subscription account in accordance with Article 295 of the Commercial Act, and that no financing shares or in-kind contributions remain unpaid. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that [BANK NAME], [BRANCH] is appointed as the company's principal depository bank. The board authorizes the representative director and the chief financial officer, jointly for amounts above KRW [THRESHOLD] and singly below, to open corporate bank accounts, execute account agreements, issue payment orders, and bind the company with respect to wire transfers and ordinary banking transactions, in compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering policy. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as statutory Auditor for the following term, with all powers conferred in the Commercial Act and the articles of incorporation. 5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND RECORDS. RESOLVED, that the company adopts the corporate seal imprinted below, that the share certificates be issued, and that the shareholder registry, minutes, and accounting records be kept at the registered office. 6. MANAGEMENT DELEGATION. RESOLVED, that the representative director is instructed to complete all post-incorporation registrations, business licensing, tax registrations and bank account activation, and report to the board at the next meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and preliminary documentation preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Register Information Center / Internet Registration Office (I-REGIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary corporate name search in the commercial register database to verify that no identical or confusingly similar name exists in Korea. Reserve the company name and determine the exact Korean legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, including the Romanized form and registered corporate seal imprint. If any foreign investor is a shareholder, prepare the investor's certificate of nationality, passport or corporate registration extract, power of attorney, and a preliminary screening under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Obtain all internal corporate approvals, such as board or parent company resolutions, required to establish a Korean subsidiary, and instruct local counsel to finalize the exact wording of the statutory objects clause for ISIC 7020 tax consulting services.
required_dossiers: Approved English/Korean company name certificate or name search report
Identity documents of all promoters and directors
Power of attorney to local counsel or incorporation agent
Foreign investor passport/certificate of nationality or corporate extract
Parent company board authorization (if relevant)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search discloses an identical or highly similar existing name, amend the proposed corporate name and refile. If foreign investor identification is incomplete, supplement with apostilled or notarized certificates before proceeding to notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of articles of incorporation and payment of subscription capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed under the Korean Notary Act; designated bank under the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language articles of incorporation containing the statutory matters enumerated in Article 289 of the Commercial Act, including corporate purposes, commercial name, total authorized shares, par value, registered office, method of public notice, and incorporation conditions. All promoters must appear before a licensed notary public or execute a power of attorney authorizing local counsel to appear, and the notary must authenticate the articles. Simultaneously, the capital of the stock corporation must be paid in full into a fixed deposit or bank account in the name of the company or the promoters' subscription account; obtain a bank certificate verifying the deposit for later application to the registration court. The choice of bank must respect the foreign exchange and declaration requirements for inbound cross-border capital if foreign funds will be remitted.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation (to be notarized)
Promoters' identification documents and powers of attorney
Capital payment certificate issued by the deposit bank
Foreign exchange or foreign investment filing proof (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests substantive corrections, revise the articles and reauthenticate. If the deposit certificate does not clearly name the prospective company or promoter, request a corrected certificate before convening the incorporation meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation organizational meeting, director election, and first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and initial shareholders constituting the statutory organization meeting under the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon full payment of the subscription price, the promoters must convene the incorporation organizational meeting without delay. The meeting shall verify the deposit certificate, declare the total number of subscribed shares and the amount of capital, elect the initial directors and a statutory auditor or establish an audit committee, and obtain the written consent of each elected officer. Keep a signed minutes record of the meeting, which must be attached to the registration application. The board of directors shall then hold its first meeting and adopt the pro-forma board resolution, including the registered office, banking authorization, and officer appointments. If the company uses a corporate seal, the seal imprint certificate and seal registration form must be signed by the representative director.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the incorporation organizational meeting
Written acceptance letters of directors and auditor
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting
Capital payment or bank deposit certificate
Corporate seal imprint specimen and seal registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an elected director or auditor declines the appointment, convene a supplemental organizational meeting and file corrected acceptances. If minutes are defective in date or signatures, re-execute and redate them before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration filing with the district court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation with the commercial registration office of the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. The application, signed by the representative director or a delegated attorney, must be submitted electronically through the Internet Registration Office or in person at the court. Attach the notarized articles, the minutes of the incorporation meeting, acceptance documents, individual seal impression certificates, and proof of the registered address such as a lease agreement or written consent by the building owner. Payment of corporate registration tax and local education tax must be made to the municipality at the same time, and the registrar examines the application for statutory compliance before issuing the certificate of registration. Upon registration, the Chusik Hoesa comes into existence as a separate legal entity.
required_dossiers: Application for corporation registration on the prescribed court form
Notarized articles of incorporation
Minutes of incorporation meeting and first board meeting
Individual seal certificates of directors and representative director
Power of attorney for the legal agent
Registered office lease contract or building owner's consent
Receipt proving payment of registration tax and local education tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order or rejection notice, promptly submit supplementary documents or a corrected application within the court-specified period, usually seven days. Pay any shortage in registration tax, or if the registrar has made a legal error, pursue an immediate appeal to the district court under the Commercial Registration Rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service business registration and corporate taxpayer identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after completion of incorporation registration, apply for the business registration certificate and corporate taxpayer registration with the competent district tax office of the National Tax Service using the unified corporate registration and business registration procedure. Present the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, power of attorney and the representative director's identification. Complete the value-added tax registration, if applicable, and obtain the corporate tax filing identification number. If the shareholders include foreign investors, submit the Foreign Investment Report to KOTRA/Invest Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank before or immediately after the capital is paid in to obtain foreign-invested company status and any available tax treatment. The tax office shall issue the stamped Business Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Notarized articles of incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Representative director's national identification or passport
Office lease agreement
Foreign investment report certificate (if foreign shareholder)
Bank account activation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business scope or representative authority, submit corrected articles and an updated representative certificate. If the foreign investment report is missing, file with KOTRA or the designated bank and provide the bank's overseas remittance receipt and certificate of capital introduction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance activation, bank account opening, and professional scope compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks, Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service, National Health Insurance Service, and local municipal government
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the corporate bank account by presenting the certificate of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, business registration certificate, and board resolution authorizing signatories. If any industrial, physical, chemical or warehouse activity is ever added to the business scope, obtain the relevant permits before commencing operations; however, for ISIC 7020 tax structuring advisory, no industrial license, Environmental Impact Assessment, or Civil Defense fire permit is applicable. The company shall nevertheless register as an employer with the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service and the National Health Insurance Service, adopt workplace risk assessments under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and maintain statutory employment records. The representative director shall then convene the first shareholders' general meeting, approve the board's founding actions, issue share certificates, and open or deposit any outstanding capital to finalize the governance framework for cross-border tax structuring engagements.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Business registration certificate
Board resolution on bank account opening and authorized signatories
Foreign investment report certificate
Employer registration forms for workers' compensation and national health insurance
Share certificates and shareholder registry
Statement confirming industrial and environmental licensing not applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank refuses to open an account due to anti-money laundering or know-your-customer concerns, supplement with source-of-funds evidence, beneficial ownership declarations, and a revised board resolution. If social insurance authorities reject employer registration, correct the corporate seal, legal existence certificate, or identification data and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 7020 is a pure consulting and professional advisory service; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity exists. General business registration is administered by the National Tax Service and ordinary business permits by the local municipal government.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for industrial operational permits. The mandatory ordinary authorization is the Business Registration Certificate issued by the National Tax Service; any tax representation or legal advisory work must also comply with the Korean Certified Tax Accountant Act and Attorney-at-Law Act professional restrictions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no environmental permit agency for pure office-based consulting; if future industrial activity arises, the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea would be the competent authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - ISIC 7020 qualifies as Category Exempt under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no full EIA report or environmental registration certificate is required for office-based tax structuring consultancy.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or emissions generation sources. Ordinary office waste must be managed under the Waste Control Act; any future physical project would require fresh environmental screening before construction or operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire safety permit, hot work certificate, structural load inspection, or dangerous goods storage approval is required for a pure consulting office. The company must, however, comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act risk assessment duties, register as an employer with the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service, and ensure the leased office building has a valid fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs clearance authority for exports: Korea Customs Service (customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Complete incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa by registering with the competent Korean district court registry office (Commercial Registration) and obtaining the corporate registration certificate. Step 2: Within 20 days of business commencement, apply for Business Registration with the competent NTS district tax office through HomeTax or in person, using the Business Registration Application under Article 8 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act. Required documents for a foreign-owned corporation include the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of the registered place of business (lease agreement or ownership document), identification and power-of-attorney documents for the responsible representative, and, where applicable, Alien Registration Card or foreign director identification. Step 3: NTS will issue a unified 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN, also known as Saupja Deungnok Beonho) which functions simultaneously as the corporate income tax TIN and the VAT registration ID; no separate VAT ID is required. Step 4: If the foreign non-resident entity itself maintains a domestic place of business or branch in Korea, the foreign corporation must separately register that domestic place of business under the Corporate Tax Act with the same competent tax office; a mere non-resident shareholder of the Chusik Hoesa has no direct NTS registration obligation unless it creates a Korean permanent establishment or taxable Korean-source activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election, and a Chusik Hoesa is an entity-level taxpayer that cannot elect pass-through or fiscally transparent treatment. Qualifying parent-subsidiary groups may elect consolidated corporate tax filing for wholly owned domestic subsidiaries under the Corporate Tax Act, but this is a group filing election, not an entity classification election. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are resolved by mandatory statutory rules under Korean tax law and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable to a Chusik Hoesa; all corporate business operators must VAT-register from business commencement regardless of turnover. The simplified taxable person regime, with an annual revenue threshold of KRW 80 million, is available only to eligible individual small businesses and cannot be used by a Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered enterprises, including a Chusik Hoesa, are required to issue electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) for taxable supplies. E-tax invoices must be transmitted to NTS through HomeTax, the Electronic Business Platform, or NTS-certified ERP API and machine-to-machine interfaces, no later than the day after issuance. The Korean system is central invoice reporting and validation rather than real-time fiscal clearance; NTS validates the supplier and recipient Business Registration Numbers and uses a central e-invoice repository with risk-scoring analytics. There is no anti-fraud digital stamp, but NTS authentication uses HomeTax credentials and public-key digital certificates for secure issuance and transmission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21(1)(1) of the Value-Added Tax Act, 0% VAT applies to exported goods where the goods are sold to a foreign buyer and physically leave the Republic of Korea. Under Article 21(1)(2) of the Value-Added Tax Act and Enforcement Decree Article 24, 0% VAT applies to services supplied to a non-resident or foreign enterprise where the service recipient is outside Korea, the service is intended for use outside Korea, and the service is not supplied in connection with a Korean permanent establishment or Korean-domestic use. The Chusik Hoesa cross-border tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory scope is eligible for 0% VAT when the recipient is a non-resident enterprise, the advisory deliverables are consumed outside Korea (or only used to manage non-Korean risks and transactions), and the service is not effectively connected with a Korean permanent establishment. The zero-rating must be substantiated by contemporaneous contractual, performance, and foreign-currency settlement evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration and Export Declaration Receipt (Export Bill of Entry) issued by Korea Customs Service evidencing physical departure of goods from Korea
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing international transport
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Receipt Confirmation issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency

For zero-rated advisory services: signed cross-border advisory contract, detailed scope and deliverable report, statement or certificate from the non-resident recipient confirming place of use outside Korea, zero-rated electronic tax invoice, and FIRC or comparable foreign-exchange receipt evidence; customs declarations are not applicable for services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service conduct post-export audits, cross-border information exchange, and documentation verification for zero-rated supplies. If the required export declaration, Bill of Lading, FIRC, foreign-currency receipt evidence, or service-use documentation is missing, inconsistent, or non-compliant with the 180-day foreign exchange settlement deadline, NTS may recharacterize the zero-rated supply as a taxable domestic supply and assess unpaid 10% VAT, additional tax liabilities generally ranging from 10% to 40% of the underreported or disallowed VAT depending on negligence or intentionality, monthly statutory interest, and penalties. Materially false tax invoices, fraudulent export zero-rating claims, or deliberate VAT evasion additionally expose responsible officers to criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, including imprisonment up to three years and fines up to three times the evaded tax amount.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the monetary and foreign-exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with foreign-exchange administration exercised by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) through delegated foreign-exchange banks and Korean Customs Service reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates an advanced current-account convertibility system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Ordinary operational inflows and outflows for consultancy services, royalties, dividends, salaries and trade settlements are free-standing, meaning a Korean Chusik Hoesa may remit or receive funds promptly through any licensed domestic foreign-exchange bank using the required FEIS purpose code and supporting documentation. Capital-account items such as equity injection, cross-border standby loans, securities purchases, and merger-related payments are not fully convertible without filing or licence; the regulator primarily relies on a negative-list model under which prohibited or restricted transactions require prior MOEF/BOK approval. Profit remittance from the Korean entity is considered current-account once the underlying earnings are realised and taxes are withheld, but foreign investors must also maintain their Foreign Investment Notice registration if they rely on FIPA rights. In practice, KRW is deliverable onshore, and non-resident KRW accounts are restricted to trade and employment purposes. The outstanding failure risk is not convertibility itself but documentary classification; a tax-structuring consultancy must pre-approve purpose codes and retain contracts, invoices, and board minutes to avoid FEIS rejection.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and BOK guidelines, exporters must cause all foreign currency export proceeds to be received no later than six months from the shipment date, although an extension to twelve months may be requested for sound transactional reasons. Once received, the proceeds must be channelled into a domestic foreign-currency account at a delegated foreign-exchange bank; there is no mandatory percentage surrender requirement, so the exporter may retain 100% of receipts in that account. If conversion to KRW is required, the bank will execute at market rate. The underlying proof set includes the customs export declaration, commercial invoice, transport document and a BOK FEIS settlement report submitted by the bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary banking rail. Offshore digital EMIs without a Korean banking licence cannot open KRW IBAN-equivalent current accounts or serve as settlement banks for a resident Chusik Hoesa. Legal barriers include the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Financial Supervisory Service licensing. Such EMIs may only act as a payment interface supported by a licensed domestic partner bank, not as a corporate treasury account or capital escrow provider. Any usage is limited to small vendor payments and must funnel into an onshore bank account to remain compliant.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is required for at least one statutory representative, namely the registered director of the Korean-incorporated entity, and for any shareholder controlling 15% or more of the equity. A power-of-attorney holder may appear only for supportive documentation after board resolution. Korean AML guidance under the Financial Action Task Force-aligned framework does not recognise remote-only onboarding for first-time entities in this elevated consultancy sector. A consular notarised power of attorney may be accepted only as supporting material, not as a substitute for the physical KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction nexus traceable through ultimate beneficial owner address or bank beneficiary history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of shareholders, board passport notarisation, source-of-wealth statement, global sanctions and PEP database clearance report, and corporate ownership tree to ultimate natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction sub-class of tax structuring advisory creates shell account scrutiny from the Financial Supervisory Service and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed tax consultancy permit, signed client engagement contracts, two-year project pipeline, audited local financial statements, physical office lease, employee payroll and social-insurance records proving substantive Korean operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-currency flows in excess of KRW 100 million equivalent or erratic credit-card-linked funding from foreign investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Declaration filed with KOTRA or the receiving bank, capital contribution remittance slip, board resolutions, FEIS purpose code classification, and independent certified public accountant capital verification certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party offshore service fees resembling profits-stripping or thin capitalisation at tax authority percentage thresholds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation including master file and local file, intercompany service agreement, margin benchmark study, payment schedule, and Korean withholding tax evidence or exemption certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must first open a designated foreign-currency corporate account at the selected Korean bank, submit a Foreign Investment Declaration to either KOTRA or the delegated bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and then remit equity funds via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 using the correct FEIS purpose code, such as 110100 classification for equity contributions, with a detailed payment reason identifying the capital injection rather than a generic current transfer. The bank performs capital verifification and issues a Foreign Investment Notification; the external auditors use the bank certificate to verify subscribed share capital and register the inflow with FEIS in order to support future dividend and exit remittances.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Corporate treasury should route outbound fee and trade settlements using SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to non-resident beneficiaries, complemented by SWIFT MT202 for large interbank cover payments. For goods movement, use Commercial Letters of Credit issued by Korean banks through correspondent networks, while Documentary Collections serve for shipments where the counterparty accepts document-as-acceptance basis. Every outbound transfer requires an underlying contract or invoice, a specific FEIS purpose code for consultancy or trade, and proof of withholding tax if the beneficiary is rendering taxable services in Korea. The bank reports each transaction to FEIS and will condition release on anti-fraud screening, so the entity must reconcile its FX purpose codes and remittance narratives with board-approved treasury instructions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/KRW forward contracts executed with a domestic foreign-exchange bank for hedging confirmed transaction-level receivables or payables, with tenors normally limited to one year.
Cross-currency swaps correlated to foreign-currency term loans or external capital expenditure when the underlying debt has been registered under FIPA and the bank obtains MOEF oversight.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not a default onshore corporate treasury vehicle for a Korean resident entity; they are permissible only under a special BOK licence for documented offshore-investment-related underlying exposures and must be booked through a separately approved treasury workstream.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and executed minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing – minutes retained at registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 3 months from fiscal year-end (e.g., by March 31 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene AGM in time may result in non-compliance penalties against directors under the Korean Commercial Act; repeated violations may serve as grounds for court-ordered dissolution or removal of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (including taxable income and tax computation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) / competent district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year companies); if a mandatory external audit is performed, deadline is extended to May 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A negligence penalty of 20% of the unreported corporate income tax (or 10% for understated amounts) plus daily late payment interest at the NTS statutory rate (base rate + 3.5% p.a.) applies; long-term non-compliance may trigger forced collection, business license revocation, and compulsory liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surcharge return (10% of corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial / city tax office where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as the corporate income tax return (within 3 months or extended to May 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty and interest are imposed at the same rate as the national corporate income tax negligence sanctions; administrative collection procedures may ensue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment enterprise annual operation and ownership report (if foreign investment has been reported)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via KOTRA / Invest Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 1,000,000, adverse impact on foreign investment incentives, and potential restrictions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements (only if the compulsory audit threshold is triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be finalized and filed before the AGM and no later than 5 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for calendar-year companies); the audit report must accompany AGM notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-appointment of an external auditor or failure to file the audit report subjects the company and responsible executives to penalties under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including fines, corrective orders, and possible extension of tax filing deadlines not being granted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a mandatory independent CPA audit is required for: (a) any Chusik Hoesa with total assets exceeding KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million) at the preceding fiscal year-end; (b) all listed stock companies; (c) financial institutions and financial holding companies; and (d) other entities specifically designated by the Act or Presidential Decree (e.g., large private companies of public interest). No separate turnover or headcount threshold exists; however, qualified SMEs below the asset threshold are exempted from mandatory audit under the SME exemption provisions of the same Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for listed companies and financial institutions. Unlisted Chusik Hoesa companies may prepare financial statements in accordance with K-IFRS or Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP). Statutory audits must be performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA) issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) and the audit report must be expressed in Korean Won.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for private Chusik Hoesa entities. A 30-day reporting window applies, however, under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA): any foreign investor acquisition or disposal of shares (change in foreign ownership) must be reported to MOTIE through KOTRA within 30 days from the transaction date. In addition, share transfers must be entered in the shareholders register to be effective against the company; no further annual confirmation is required by commercial law. For AML purposes, companies engaged in financial transaction advisory services may be required to keep up-to-date UBO identification records accessible to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU), but this is an on-demand inspection rather than a recurrent annual filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders registration ledger under Article 396 of the Korean Commercial Act)
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board of Directors' Meetings
Register of Charges/Mortgages (including secured and collateral records kept for any asset-based financing or corporate bond issuance, in line with Korean commercial practice)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500 - $2,000 per annum depending on location (Seoul premium; regional lower)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 - $15,000 per engagement for a typical small-to-mid-sized Chusik Hoesa, depending on complexity and total assets

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (progressive: 10% up to KRW 200M; 20% above KRW 200M to KRW 20B; 22% above KRW 20B to KRW 300B; 25% above KRW 300B) plus 10% local income tax surtax, resulting in a top aggregate effective rate of 27.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays and incentives under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act (STTCA) include: 50–100% corporate income tax reductions for new growth/engine industries in free economic zones; 5-year/2-year 50% deduction for foreign-invested high-tech businesses in foreign investment zones; patent box regime (tax reduction of 50% on qualifying IP income for SMEs, subject to conditions); R&D tax credits up to 30–50% of qualifying R&D expenditures; and one-year immediate expensing for certain facilities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 10 (Corporate Tax Return) filed via HomeTax (홈택스) electronic filing system operated by the National Tax Service (NTS). Additional schedules include Form 12 (Tax Base and Tax Calculation) and Form 13 (Reconciliation Statements).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (statutory tax period is the fiscal year; required interim prepayments are made semi-annually every August 31 and November 30).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For the fiscal year ending December 31, the corporate income tax return must be filed and paid within 3 months from the fiscal year-end (i.e., by March 31 of the following year). For non-calendar year-end entities, within 3 months after each fiscal year-end. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, it is extended to the next business day. A written extension of up to 1 month may be granted upon application, provided the NTS approves (limited to certain conditions, e.g., overseas business).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity's unique 10-digit tax registration number issued by the district tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the permanent business registration number of the Korean Chusik Hoesa. For foreign-invested entities, the same number is used; any foreign branch or permanent establishment should use its separate Korean registration number. Incorrect entry triggers rejection in HomeTax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the corporation as registered in the Korean Commercial Register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must exactly match the Korean name registered with the court registry. Foreign name can be added in parentheses. Mismatches cause processing delays and may raise AML scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Starting and ending dates of the tax period (commonly January 1 to December 31).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should ensure the fiscal year aligns with the parent company's consolidated year-end only if permitted under the Corporate Tax Act. A change of fiscal year requires prior NTS approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue, including all domestic and overseas supply of services, as stated in the profit and loss statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a cross-border tax structuring consultancy, include service fees from related and unrelated parties. Exclude VAT (report separately on VAT return). If revenue from exports is tax-exempt, document zero-rated export receipts. Warn: All foreign-source revenue derived from consulting services performed in Korea is subject to Korean corporate tax as domestic-source income under Article 9 of the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income less deductible expenses, before tax adjustments and carryforward loss deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust book income for tax-accrual differences. Non-resident-owned corporations must arm's-length pricing under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Disallowed deductions, such as entertainment expenses exceeding statutory limits, must be added back. Any intercompany management fees must be substantiated by actual services and benefit tests to avoid denial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying all deductions, non-taxable income, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply carryforward losses up to 10 years (per recent reform). For foreign-invested companies, ensure the loss carryforward does not involve a change-in-control shell acquisition; otherwise, NTS may disallow the carryforward under anti-abuse rules. If the entity is a shell or lacks economic substance, the tax basis may be recalculated under CFC rules (Article 63 of the International Tax Adjustment Act).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal tax computed by applying progressive corporate income tax rates to the tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Progressive rates apply: 10% for taxable income up to KRW 200M; 20% for KRW 200M–20B; 22% for KRW 20B–300B; 25% above KRW 300B. Additionally, compute 10% local income tax (지방소득세) on the corporate income tax amount for the same return, filed separately with the local government but electronically coordinated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (가산세 - Additions to Tax and Penalties)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Penalty amounts calculated for underreporting, overstating deductions, late filing, and other compliance failures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must be extremely careful: underreporting income triggers a penalty equal to 10% (or 40% when misreporting related to international outbound transactions) of the difference. Omitted transfer pricing income may trigger a 20% net adjustment penalty plus unremitted foreign information reporting penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowed tax credits (R&D, foreign tax credits, early filing, and investment credits) that directly reduce the computed tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When claiming a unilateral foreign tax credit for taxes paid abroad, include Form 35 and complete the 'Foreign Tax Credit' schedule. Korea prohibits double deduction; credit limited to the Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income. For DTA treaty relief on dividends/interest/royalty, ensure the Beneficial Owner certificate is obtained and attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after all credits and prepayments, to be remitted to the NTS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wire the amount due with a bank reference. Any foreign currency payment must be converted at the NTS-recognized exchange rate for the final day of the fiscal year. Late payment incurs 0.025% per day surcharge. Do not offset any tax withheld at source unless properly recorded; treaty WHT on outbound dividends must be independently paid when remitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failures to file or pay corporate tax trigger: (i) late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax (or 0.03% per day up to 20% for underreporting); (ii) a per-day surcharge of 0.025% for late payment; (iii) 10% penalty for omission of a required schedule; (iv) 40% penalty for intentional underreporting of non-arm's-length transactions with foreign related parties; and (v) for willful evasion exceeding KRW 100M/300M thresholds, criminal prosecution under Article 128 of the Corporate Tax Act with imprisonment up to 3 years (or 5 years when the amount exceeds KRW 500M) plus fines up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (15% corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax on the dividend income for non-resident shareholders; for a non-resident entity, a 20% final withholding tax applies unless a treaty reduces it). Additional 10% of the dividend amount may be withheld as surtax if the dividend is an income-sourced in Korea.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Tax Treaty (DTA) reduced rate: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority of the shareholder's resident jurisdiction, issued for the relevant fiscal year; (2) complete and sign the Korean 'Verification of Beneficial Ownership' form (Form 21 from the NTS or the relevant DTA-specific form); (3) submit these documents to the Korean withholding agent (the Korean subsidiary) before the dividend distribution date, or apply for a refund via the NTS within 5 years from the date of tax collection if withholding was already applied; (4) the beneficial owner cannot be a conduit or an agent and must have the power to the income's benefit; (5) retain supporting documentation showing no pass-through arrangement and meeting any minimum holding period (e.g., for OECD-aligned treaties, typically 365-day period); (6) file the relevant treaty reduction claim in the tax return period. For Korea's treaty with most counterparties, the dividend withholding rate is 5–15% depending on the ownership percentage (e.g., 10% or 15%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 25% on outbound interest (22% for interest paid to non-residents not attributable to a permanent establishment, plus 2% local tax). Treaty reduction typically to 10–15%, and no tax on interest under certain treaties (e.g., with some jurisdictions). Royalties: statutory 25% (or 20% under certain service/consultancy characterization), including payments for the use of intellectual property, technical know-how, or trademark. Under DTA, royalties are generally reduced to 10–15%; some treaties apply 0% for technical assistance or professional services classified as business profits (only if no permanent establishment). A withholding tax exemption may apply for royalties paid for the use of, or the right to use, industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment under the OECD framework or specific DTA. Thailand, Singapore, and China treaties often cap royalty WHT at 10–15%. All payments must be supported by proper contracts and economic substance evidence to avoid reclassification as a sham.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Transfer Pricing (TP) documentation thresholds per the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA): Local File (per-entity) must be prepared when intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 10 billion for services/goods/year (or KRW 10 billion for all intercompany transaction categories combined). Master File required when the consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and intercompany foreign transactions exceed KRW 10 billion. Simplified documentation thresholds may apply for transactions under KRW 5 billion per counterparty, but a written rationale is still recommended. Thresholds are per each cross-border related-party transaction category (sales, purchases, loans, intangibles, services).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not have a formal 'Economic Substance Regulation' (ESR) as in offshore jurisdictions, but the doctrine is embedded in the corporate tax general anti-abuse rules (Article 52 of the Corporate Tax Act) and the CFC rules (Article 63 of LCITA). For a Korean Chusik Hoesa, the 'substance over form' test requires that the company maintains real business premises, employees, contract sign-off authority, bank accounts, and management functions in Korea. For a holding or advisory entity, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) must be performed in Korea – not merely receiving invoices and issuing receipts. The NTS applies the 'economic ownership' principle to deny treaty benefits or tax deductions to a Korean entity that is a shell or lacks the capacity to perform the consulting services. The OECD's BEPS Action 6 and Korea's treaty abuse limitation on benefits (LOB) provisions demand that the entity demonstrates active business and real value creation. If substance is insufficient, the NTS may deem the Korean entity to be a 'paper company,' recharacterize income, and levy a 40% penalty plus liability upto the personal assets of the directors.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.transfer_pricing_penalty: Additional penalty of 20% of the net understated tax arising from TP adjustments if arm's-length price not documented; a 30% penalty if no TP documentation at all; and a 5% per-day penalty for failure to submit required TP reports.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Artificial Shell Structuring (Piercing Corporate Veil under Corporate Tax Act Art. 52 and Criminal Act Art. 347)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa is set up with no office, no employees, and no real consulting functions, but invoices international service fees (purported management advice) to related parties, generating deductible expenses that are actually used to shift profits abroad. The company does not file the corporate income tax return or files a nil return while large intercompany payments flow to a tax-haven affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS recharacterizes the transactions, disallows deductions, imposes 40% penalties on the underreported income, and charges up to KRW 200M in additional taxes. Criminal referral for intentional fraudulent tax evasion under Article 128 of the Corporate Tax Act and Article 347 of the Criminal Act (Fraud).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The National Tax Collection Act (Article 28) allows the NTS to pierce the corporate veil and impose secondary tax liability on a director who was grossly negligent or abusively used the corporation as a conduit for tax evasion. The director's bank accounts may be frozen, and a travel ban ('blacklisting') is issued through the NTS and Immigration Service to prevent flight. Criminal conviction for tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act (Article 9) carries imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 3 times the tax evaded. The director's personal assets, including the residence, are subject to civil restitution orders to recover the unpaid tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud and Concealment of Intercompany Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean advisory entity conducts transactions with a foreign related party (e.g., sells consulting services to a Hong Kong affiliate) at a price far below arm's-length, effectively shifting KRW 30 billion of taxable income outside Korea. The directors produce bogus invoices and create a false written contractual discount to justify the price, and they intentionally omit mandatory Master/Local File documentation and the 'Schedule of Related Party Transactions.'
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS adjusts the transfer price to arm's-length, imposes an income adjustment, and adds a 40% negligence penalty on the underreported amount (under Article 3 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs). The CPA who signed the false documentation may be referred to the regulatory authorities, and the firm's license suspended. If the adjustment exceeds KRW 50 billion, the case is automatically referred to the Public Prosecutors' Office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed the false TP documentation are personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under the doctrine of 'piercing the corporate veil' in the National Tax Collection Act and the Corporate Tax Act. Criminal indictment under Article 347 of the Criminal Act can lead to imprisonment up to 10 years if the fraud amount is extremely high. A restraining order is placed on their assets, and a travel ban is issued preventing them from leaving Korea. Courts have awarded restitution to the NTS for the entire tax, penalties, and interest out of the director's personal property.
